messages:
sana_perf: Quick heads-up: ran end-to-end host-side profile for a synthetic 8k-token burst workload. Host CPU dominated by pre-tokenization and transport framing. KV hit lower than expected.

jules_sre: paste perf snippets and the exact bench command? curious if syscall noise or CPU work. :eyes: 

sana_perf: Command: `bench/runner --clients=200 --seq=8192 --duration=30s --model=redwood/7b:fp16`.
Flame summary (host wall avg/request):
```
baseline-2026-03-19
 total host wall: 14.2ms
 - http decode/frame: 4.9ms
 - pre-tokenize (utf8 fast/nibble): 5.8ms
 - tokenizer CPU: 2.1ms
 - grpc writev/socket flush: 1.4ms
 - syscall/writev count ~45/request
kv: hit=62% miss=38% (tail misses concentrated on shards 3,7)
```

sana_perf: Built mini-pretokenizer shim: moves ascii prefix handling into fast-path.
```
shim-run:
 total: 10.6ms (-25%)
 - shim ascii fast-path: 1.2ms
 - tokenizer heavy path: 2.3ms
 - http decode/frame: 4.6ms (-6%)
 - writev ~18/request
 kv hit ~60%
```

ben_eng: Small CPU wins can expose grpc/http tail. We saw writev aggregation drop to single writes when messages hit a threshold. Which gRPC flags? any send buffer tuning?

alex_runtime: Runtime note: we pick "short-seq" kernel for seq <64. It reduces vector ops but increases mem copies and host preproc pressure. Try raising threshold to 96.

sana_perf: Ran branch perf/kernel-threshold-96. Early: total 9.8ms, tokenizer 2.0ms, writev ~12/request. Collecting pprof+flames.

mike_devex: Enable socket coalescing (SO_SNDBUF bump + TCP_CORK / MSG_MORE heuristics) should reduce syscalls. Try shim + coalesce.

sana_perf: Shim + coalesce + kt96 microcanary (50 qps, 5m):
```
microcanary-1
 total: 8.7ms (-39% vs baseline)
 writev ~6/request
 kv hit 63%
 p95 improved 32%
 host net cpu down ~18%
```

jules_sre: Good. How about batching? continuous batching heuristics might interact and change tail.

sana_perf: With heuristic-batch (prefer batch for seq <512): throughput up but median latency +0.7ms due to queueing.
```
no-batch: p50=30ms p95=120ms rps=520
heuristic-batch: p50=30.7ms p95=92ms rps=680
```

ben_eng: Tail vs throughput trade. Suggest dynamic cutoff: enable batching only if estimated queue delay <0.8ms (derive from inflight counters).

alex_runtime: Also seeing KV evictions on two shards. Per-shard eviction metrics would tell if remap or more shards needed.

sana_perf: Added per-shard metrics: shard 3/7 eviction+reinsert ~78%. Plan: remap to 16 shards (was 8) and re-run.

mike_devex: For rollout: 10% canary tag: `X-RW-Perf-Variant: shim+coalesce+kt96+shards16`. Console will attach perf panel and auto rollback if p95 regresses >15%.

deploy-bot: Canary created: perf/ingress/1799004321-canary-10% tag shim+coalesce+kt96+shards16. Monitoring enabled.

sana_perf: Next steps: 1) confirm structured-output correctness, 2) measure memory from shard increase, 3) implement dynamic-batch cutoff in routing. Will post pprofs when done.

jules_sre: Ping me for merge/perf CI. If canary is green we'll do phased rollout.

sana_perf: Summary: pretokenizer fast-path + kernel threshold bump + socket coalesce + shard increase => ~35-40% host-side wall reduction for this workload. Small batching tail we can mitigate with dynamic cutoff. Thanks all :rocket:
